_comment: The machine-checkable definition of pilot-done (issue #193). One entry per pilot-critical behavior, distilled from docs/pilot-launch/15-full-product-requirements-register.md (IDs are that register's IDs; it remains the full normative source). passes flips to true ONLY by a verifier session that is not the implementer, with evidence linked. JSON, not markdown, on purpose: checklists in prose get tampered with; a diff to this file is reviewable.

entries.requirement: Gmail mailbox ingestion, classification, and status mutation are disabled
entries.oracle: No mail scopes, tokens, schedules, or routes exist

entries.requirement: Anonymous users reach only public/auth/legal/support routes
Pending users get a holding state with no product data or commands
Ownership derives from authenticated context inside authoritative locks
Two users are isolated across DB, RPC, storage, cache, export, events, workers, support
Google sign-in neither implies nor requests Gmail mailbox consent
Postgres is the sole authority for identity-linked product state
Production performs zero Sheet read/write/sync/reconciliation operations
Every mutation uses an authenticated idempotent command/RPC
Versioned resources reject stale writes and preserve drafts
Today badge, count, and rows use one owner-scoped actionable query contract
Applications support add, import, manual status, notes, activity, export — without Gmail
Human application status is never overwritten by automation
Coverage reflects actual Postgres subscriptions and per-user runs
Profile supports any US job family/seniority/work model without persona defaults
